reason: FINDINGS entry 1: gofmt aligns consecutive struct fields, tags, const values and trailing comments. A rule cannot inspect a sibling's rendered width. Every hunk in this file is that padding; none is a package defect.

FINDINGS entry 1: the only difference is gofmt padding `_` to align with `KB` on `=`. Checked the rest of the iota forms (implicit repetition, shifts); they match. Not a package bug wearing alignment clothing.
FINDINGS entry 1: the only difference is `ID` padded to align with `Name`/`Tags`. The rest of the kitchen (imports, map literal, method, range-for) matches.
FINDINGS entry 1: the only difference is `Value` padded to align with `Children`. Nested composite literals already match because they use source-mirroring breaks, not alignment.
FINDINGS entry 1: the only differences are struct field/tag column padding on Model. Interpreted/raw/rune literals, escapes and concatenation already match (verbatim + binary +).
FINDINGS entry 1: remaining hunks are field/tag alignment on Base, User and Permissions. Empty `struct{}` and compact `struct{ left, right int }` now match; those were package bugs and are gone.

The only remaining hunk is `struct{` vs `struct {` on a one-field broken type. gofmt writes `struct{ T }` when the source is one line and `struct {\n T\n}` when it is broken: the space before `{` is present iff the body breaks. srcline before `{` sees `{` itself (always same-line); `sp` is unconditional. Doc::IfBreak exists for paren/trail but is not an opcode. Adding one for this space on two files is the house-style bad trade. Empty and compact one-field forms already match.

Two remaining hunks, both design limits. (1) Same one-field `struct{` vs `struct {` as functions.go: no opcode emits a space only when the body is source-broken. (2) `len(s.items)-1` is tight inside `[]` and spaced everywhere else (gofmt `a[1-2]` stays tight; `f(1-2)` becomes `f(1 - 2)`). Tightness is ancestor context (FINDINGS entry 2); binary_expression cannot ask whether it sits in an index. Type-only parameter spaces and type-set `|` spaces were package bugs and are fixed.

FINDINGS entry 2: gofmt spaces the loosest operators in an expression and writes tighter ones flush (`a + b*c`, `a+b < c+d`). flatten+precedence can keep same-tightness chains together but the child `*` node cannot know it sits under `+`. A when-on-operator-type rule that always tightens `*` would break standalone `a * b * c` and `a &^ b` (gofmt spaces those). Verified by running gofmt on uniform vs mixed vs index forms.

Four remaining hunks, none package-expressible. (1) `a + b*2` mixed-precedence tightness: same FINDINGS entry 2 as operators.go. (2) `if (x != nil)` vs `if x != nil`: gofmt strips condition parens; parenthesized_expression cannot ask its parent (entry 2) and there is no consume-without-emit opcode. (3) `((1))` vs `(1)`: same token-deletion gap; transparent_wrappers lets gate 3 allow the drop but the package cannot skip `(`/`)`. (4) mid-line semicolons: srctrail would strip them but also inserts `;` between every later line-broken decl, breaking idempotence. Linearity forbids a skip opcode. Token-level spacing, indent and the empty `func weird()` already match.
